title: Evolved tissues show delayed gratification as an unselected free lunch

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Evolved tissues show delayed gratification as an unselected free lunch

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In the evolved neural cellular automaton, the tissue temporarily moves away from its target pattern to remove misplaced cells and then returns (delayed gratification in the TAME framework), and since neither this nor long-term maintenance was selected for, such capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems can emerge as a 'free lunch' without direct selection.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L 2023, The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis › Discussion

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Interestingly, neither of these things were directly selected for during the evolutionary cycle, revealing how some capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems can emerge as a kind of ‘free lunch’, without direct selection pressure [2,88].

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Pio-Lopez L, Bischof J, LaPalme JV, Levin M, “The scaling of goals from cellular to anatomical homeostasis: an evolutionary simulation, experiment and analysis”, Interface focus (2023), doi:10.1098/rsfs.2022.0072; section “Discussion”. Scope: In silico 2D neural cellular automata evolved for the French flag problem; multi-scale homeostatic systems

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-goals-16: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.82

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The trajectory, maintenance, and selection objective are inspectable in public code and testable by reruns and controls. The broader assertion about multiscale systems generally exceeds this model, but the stated in-model result is resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Audit the fitness function and evolutionary protocol, then rerun evolved controllers under perturbations and measure temporary increases in target error followed by recovery and long-term maintenance. Compare against unevolved and explicitly selected controls to test whether these abilities arose without direct selection.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Indirect selection or correlation with the fitness objective may explain the capability.

'Delayed gratification' is an interpretive label for a trajectory.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The excursion away from the target and the contents of the fitness function can be checked by running and reading the public model, which is analysis. The repository does not contain the published long runs, and the step from this fitness function to unselected capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems generally is outside what one simulation decides. Endpoint versus cumulative fitness is a real ambiguity in the test.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In runs of the evolved tissue, measure distance to the French-flag target over time and read the fitness function in the code. A transient increase in distance while misplaced cells are removed, followed by return, in a model whose fitness does not reward that excursion or long-term maintenance, would support the simulation result; monotonic approach, or a fitness term that penalizes intermediate error, would refute the unselected-excursion reading.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The committed script is a short demonstration configuration, so it is not a replay of the published 1000-step runs.

Whether intermediate error is invisible to selection depends on whether fitness is an endpoint score or a time integral, which has to be read out of the model class rather than a deposited results table.
